chill.title: Follow Beargrass Creek at the Nature Center
chill.description: Forty-one acres of protected urban woodland beside the zoo, with boardwalks over the creek and a bird blind almost nobody uses.
chill.bonus: Sit in the bird blind until you have identified three species.

chill.title: Wander Yew Dell Botanical Gardens
chill.description: A former nurseryman's estate east of the city, with a stone castle folly, a walled garden and serious plant collections in a small footprint.
chill.bonus: Find the castle and walk all the way around it.

chill.title: Walk St. James Court in Old Louisville
chill.description: The largest contiguous Victorian neighbourhood in the United States, with gas lamps, a fountain court and pedestrian walkways running behind the houses.
chill.bonus: Find one of the hidden walking courts behind the main street.

chill.title: Take the Big Four Lawn at Waterfront Park
chill.description: Eighty-five acres of riverfront green between downtown and the Ohio, with a swing set facing the water that people queue for.
chill.bonus: Get one of the riverfront swings and stay on it for a full twenty minutes.

chill.title: Take the Long Way Down Bardstown Road
chill.description: The Highlands' main artery, a couple of miles of record shops, vintage racks, coffee counters and dive bars that reward walking rather than driving.
chill.bonus: Walk from Baxter to Douglass Loop without getting in a car.

chill.title: See the Water Tower at Louisville's WaterWorks
chill.description: The oldest ornamental water tower in the world, a Greek Revival column ringed with statues on the riverbank, with a small museum in the pumping station beside it.
chill.bonus: Count the statues on the colonnade.

chill.title: Sit Out a Morning at Sunergos
chill.description: A South Preston roastery and cafe open from half six, with the kind of unhurried room that makes a long morning feel like a plan.
chill.bonus: Stay for a second drink and do not open your laptop.

chill.title: Walk the Cast-Iron Facades of Whiskey Row
chill.description: A block of 19th-century cast-iron warehouse fronts on West Main, saved from demolition and now holding distilleries, hotels and a museum behind the original facades.
chill.bonus: Pick out the oldest building on the block from the architecture alone.

chill.title: Browse Carmichael's on Bardstown Road
chill.description: Louisville's oldest independent bookshop, open since 1978, with a well-run author event calendar and staff picks worth taking seriously.
chill.bonus: Buy whichever book has the longest handwritten staff card.

chill.title: Find Ali and the Colonel at Cave Hill
chill.description: A 296-acre Victorian arboretum-cemetery where Muhammad Ali and Colonel Sanders are buried a short walk apart, among lakes, swans and enormous old trees.
chill.bonus: Find both graves without looking up directions more than once.

adventure.title: Paddle the Floyds Fork Canoe Trail
adventure.description: A flat-water creek trail running the length of the Parklands, with put-ins at every park and herons the entire way.
adventure.bonus: Paddle a full section end to end without portaging.

adventure.title: Drop In at the Louisville Extreme Park
adventure.description: Forty thousand square feet of concrete under the I-65 overpass, open twenty-four hours, with a twenty-four-foot full pipe that draws skaters from across the country.
adventure.bonus: Stay long enough to watch someone actually ride the full pipe.

adventure.title: Zip 100 Feet Above the Mega Cavern Floor
adventure.description: The world's only fully underground zipline course — six lines and two challenge bridges strung across a former limestone mine beneath the city.
adventure.bonus: Do the longest line without grabbing the harness once.

adventure.title: Walk the Big Four Bridge into Indiana
adventure.description: A converted 1895 railway bridge with a spiral ramp at each end, carrying you on foot across the Ohio River into another state and back.
adventure.bonus: Cross to Jeffersonville, get something there, and walk back.

adventure.title: Take the Overnight Tour at Waverly Hills
adventure.description: A Gothic former tuberculosis hospital with a body chute and a reputation as one of the most haunted buildings in America, open for two-hour night tours.
adventure.bonus: Go down the body chute and stay to the far end.

adventure.title: Hike the Siltstone Trail in Jefferson Memorial Forest
adventure.description: The largest municipal urban forest in the United States, with over sixty miles of trail and knobs steep enough to feel like real Kentucky.
adventure.bonus: Take the full Siltstone traverse rather than an out-and-back.

adventure.title: Hike to the Rose Island Ruins
adventure.description: A 1920s amusement park abandoned after the 1937 flood, reached on foot through Charlestown State Park — pool shells, a zoo gate and stone steps still in the woods.
adventure.bonus: Find the old swimming pool foundation before you turn back.

adventure.title: Climb the Iroquois Park Overlook
adventure.description: Another Olmsted park, this one built around a wooded knob, with a summit road and a stone overlook giving the widest view of Louisville there is.
adventure.bonus: Walk up rather than drive, and get there for sunset.

adventure.title: Day Trip the Arches of Red River Gorge
adventure.description: Ninety minutes east, a canyon system with more than a hundred natural sandstone arches and some of the best sport climbing in the country.
adventure.bonus: Stand on top of Natural Bridge rather than just under it.

adventure.title: Cross All Four Parklands of Floyds Fork
adventure.description: Four linked parks strung along twenty miles of creek on the city's eastern edge, connected by a paved park drive and a canoe trail.
adventure.bonus: Get from Beckley Creek to Broad Run under your own power.

adventure.title: Find the Forest Giants at Bernheim
adventure.description: Sixteen thousand acres of research forest and arboretum, home to three enormous recycled-wood giants hidden in the trees and a canopy walk above the ravine.
adventure.bonus: Find all three giants in one visit without asking for directions.

adventure.title: Ride the Otter Creek Trails
adventure.description: Two thousand acres on the Ohio River with the best mountain biking within an hour of Louisville, from flowy green loops to genuinely rocky black.
adventure.bonus: Ride the full outer loop in one go.

adventure.title: Ride a Stretch of the Louisville Loop
adventure.description: A paved trail being built to ring the entire city, with the riverfront section already running for miles past parks, locks and the odd barge.
adventure.bonus: Ride until you have no idea what neighbourhood you are in.

adventure.title: Run the Scenic Loop at Cherokee Park
adventure.description: Frederick Law Olmsted's Louisville masterpiece, with a 2.4-mile loop road split between cars and people, and enough hills to make it honest work.
adventure.bonus: Do the full loop and take the Hogan's Fountain detour on the way.

adventure.title: Walk the Devonian Fossil Beds at Falls of the Ohio
adventure.description: One of the largest exposed Devonian fossil beds in the world, 390 million years old, walkable when the river is low — straight across the bridge from downtown.
adventure.bonus: Find and photograph three different coral fossils.

adventure.title: Ride the Underground Bike Park
adventure.description: Forty-five trails, jump lines, a pump track and dual slalom, all 100 feet below ground at a constant sixty degrees no matter the weather outside.
adventure.bonus: Clear a jump line you would not attempt on a normal trail.

culture.title: Get Your Name on a Slugger Bat
culture.description: A working bat factory behind a 120-foot bat leaning on the building, where the tour ends with a miniature bat and you can order a full-size one with your name burned in.
culture.bonus: Hold a bat used by a player you have actually heard of.

culture.title: See What KMAC Has Up on Whiskey Row
culture.description: A contemporary art museum on West Main built around craft and material, with shows that change often and a shop worth the visit alone.
culture.bonus: Buy something from a Kentucky maker in the museum shop.

culture.title: Start the Bourbon Trail at the Frazier
culture.description: The official Kentucky Bourbon Trail welcome centre, wrapped around a history museum that is far better than it needs to be.
culture.bonus: Pick up the trail passport and get your first stamp the same day.

culture.title: Walk the Backside at Churchill Downs
culture.description: The Kentucky Derby Museum sits at the track itself, and the walking tour takes you onto the grounds under the twin spires whether or not there is racing.
culture.bonus: Stand at the finish line and picture the crowd.

culture.title: Get in the Coopers at Lynn Family Stadium
culture.description: A purpose-built soccer ground in Butchertown shared by Louisville City FC and NWSL side Racing Louisville, with a supporters' end that does not sit down.
culture.bonus: Stand in the supporters' section and last the whole match on your feet.

culture.title: Take the Full Tour at Roots 101
culture.description: An African American history museum on North First Street tracing the story from West Africa through slavery to civil rights, built largely from one man's collection.
culture.bonus: Ask a staff member which object in the building means the most to them.

culture.title: Spend an Afternoon at the Speed Art Museum
culture.description: Kentucky's oldest and largest art museum, on the University of Louisville campus, with a glass North Building wrapped around a Beaux-Arts original.
culture.bonus: Find one work in the contemporary wing you would defend to someone who hated it.

culture.title: Work Through the Six Core Principles at the Ali Center
culture.description: Muhammad Ali's own museum in his home city, built around his six principles rather than his record, with a speed bag you are allowed to hit.
culture.bonus: Do the shadow-boxing station in front of other people.

social.title: Start at the Evan Williams Bourbon Experience
social.description: An artisanal distillery and immersive tour on Whiskey Row that walks you through Kentucky's whole bourbon story, which makes it the right first stop.
social.bonus: Do this one first, then compare every later tour against it.

social.title: Drink at the Copper Still in Michter's Fort Nelson
social.description: A meticulously restored 19th-century building on Main with a gleaming copper pot still downstairs and one of the best cocktail bars in the city upstairs.
social.bonus: Skip the tour queue and just take a seat at the bar instead.

social.title: See a Show Under the Louisville Palace Ceiling
social.description: A 1928 Spanish Baroque movie palace on Fourth Street with a ceiling painted as a night sky and a year-round calendar of touring music and comedy.
social.bonus: Look up before the lights go down and find the star ceiling.

social.title: Watch Barrels Being Made at Old Forester
social.description: The only distillery on Whiskey Row with its own working cooperage, where the tour includes barrels being charred in front of you.
social.bonus: Stand close enough to the barrel char to feel the heat.

social.title: Drink Belgian Beer in a Church at Holy Grale
social.description: A century-old Highlands church turned beer bar, with a deep Belgian list, a stained-glass room and an interconnected beer garden out the back.
social.bonus: Drink one Belgian style you have never ordered before.

social.title: Play Pinball Between Bands at Zanzabar
social.description: A Germantown bar and music venue with one of the better pinball collections in the Midwest and a stage that books local and touring acts most nights.
social.bonus: Win a free game on any machine in the room.

social.title: Go Down the Rabbit Hole
social.description: A glass-and-steel distillery in NuLu built like a cathedral to distillation, with tours capped small enough to actually ask questions.
social.bonus: Ask the guide a question the tour script does not cover.

social.title: Taste Sweet Mash at Kentucky Peerless
social.description: A family distillery revived after Prohibition killed the original, running a sweet mash process almost nobody else uses, a block off Whiskey Row.
social.bonus: Get someone to explain sweet mash versus sour mash and be able to repeat it.

social.title: Do the Urban Bourbon Trail on Foot
social.description: Dozens of downtown bars and distilleries linked into one walkable trail, with enough of them on Whiskey Row that you never need a car.
social.bonus: Hit four stops in one night without getting in a vehicle.

social.title: Take the Rooftop at Copper & Kings
social.description: A Butchertown brandy distillery that plays loud music to its ageing barrels, with a rooftop bar looking straight back at the downtown skyline.
social.bonus: Do the tour first, then take the same spirit up to the roof.

social.title: Stay for the Late Set at The Silver Dollar
social.description: A converted 1930s firehouse on Frankfort Avenue running Bakersfield country on vinyl, a deep American whiskey list and a kitchen that stays open late.
social.bonus: Request something off the jukebox and let the bar hear it.

social.title: Take the Finishing Tour at Angel's Envy
social.description: A full production distillery on Main Street where the tour follows grain to glass and ends on the port-barrel finish that made the brand.
social.bonus: Taste the finished bourbon against the unfinished and say which you prefer.

foodie.title: Graze the Stalls at Logan Street Market
foodie.description: Louisville's only public market, with eight-plus food concepts and five bars under one roof in Shelby Park, including a James Beard-nominated chef's counter.
foodie.bonus: Eat from three different stalls in one visit.

foodie.title: Book the Tasting Menu at 610 Magnolia
foodie.description: The Old Louisville dining room that rebuilt Southern fine dining from the inside out, still running a set menu in a converted corner storefront.
foodie.bonus: Take the full menu rather than asking for substitutions.

foodie.title: Eat Schnitzel in Schnitzelburg at Monnik
foodie.description: A Burnett Avenue brewery with a genuinely good kitchen, doing Dutch and German plates alongside beer brewed in the back.
foodie.bonus: Pair whatever you order with the beer the bartender picks.

foodie.title: Take the Patio at Naive
foodie.description: Under new ownership with a Latin-leaning menu, this Butchertown room has a patio that fills as fast as the cocktail list does.
foodie.bonus: Sit outside and order two things you cannot identify.

foodie.title: Take a Pour-Over at Quills Coffee
foodie.description: Louisville's own roastery with half a dozen cafes across the city, and the kind of bar staff who will talk you through the origin if you let them.
foodie.bonus: Ask which single origin they are most excited about and order that.

foodie.title: Eat a Hot Brown Where It Was Invented
foodie.description: The Brown Hotel invented the open-faced turkey, bacon and Mornay Hot Brown in 1926, and still serves it in the lobby bar under the original ceiling.
foodie.bonus: Finish the whole thing without leaving the bread.

foodie.title: Wait for a Table at Hammerheads
foodie.description: A tiny, dark Schnitzelburg basement doing smoked lamb nachos and duck tacos, with no reservations and a queue that forms before it opens.
foodie.bonus: Order the lamb nachos even if someone tells you not to.

foodie.title: Pick Your Heat Level at Royals Hot Chicken
foodie.description: Nashville-style hot chicken on East Market, with a heat scale that goes further than most people should take it and sides that justify the trip alone.
foodie.bonus: Order one level hotter than you were going to.

foodie.title: Get a Booth at Jack Fry's
foodie.description: A Highlands room that has been open since 1933, all dark wood and boxing photographs, with live piano and a lamb chop people order without reading the menu.
foodie.bonus: Go on a night with live piano and sit near it.

foodie.title: Take the Upstairs Room at Butchertown Grocery
foodie.description: A corner-store building in Butchertown turned into a proper restaurant, with a cocktail bar upstairs that most first-timers never find.
foodie.bonus: Find the upstairs bar and have one drink there before dinner.

foodie.title: Eat Under the Art at Proof on Main
foodie.description: The restaurant inside 21c's flagship museum hotel, where a serious bourbon list and Kentucky bison share a room with rotating contemporary art.
foodie.bonus: Walk the hotel's free galleries before or after you eat.

foodie.title: Order Off Anthony Lamas's Menu at Seviche
foodie.description: Latin technique run through Southern ingredients by one of Louisville's most-nominated chefs, with a ceviche list worth working through.
foodie.bonus: Order two ceviches and compare them properly.

8ball.title: Eight Ball: Cross the River and Come Back Different
8ball.description: Walk the Big Four into Indiana with no plan, eat and drink entirely on the Jeffersonville side, and walk back after dark.
8ball.bonus: Do the whole crossing and the return on foot, no rideshare either way.

8ball.title: Eight Ball: Underground First, Bourbon After
8ball.description: Spend the morning a hundred feet below Louisville — zipline, bike park or tram, your pick — then surface and drink your way along Whiskey Row.
8ball.bonus: Tell the first bartender where you have just been and see what they pour you.
